solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dog dirt and nothing else keeps Georgia grumpy

indicators.note: something that keeps another thing holds it inside, so one piece sits within the others

blocks.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
mud is wet dirt
GE is the international code for Georgia
only means and nothing else

explanation.surface: Someone stepping in dog mess while visiting Georgia turns sour.
explanation.walkthrough: The dog and dirt words joined with 'and nothing else' make one long string that keeps Georgia's code tucked inside, just before its final four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A curmudgeon is a bad-tempered old person, so curmudgeonly behaviour is irritable and grumpy.

clue.text: Calcium cook often upped in queen's diet?

indicators.note: in a down clue, upped means the words are set going upwards, read from bottom to top

blocks.note: Ca is the chemical symbol for calcium
to do food is to cook it
oft is an old word for often

explanation.surface: A dietary question about calcium in the Queen's meals, cooked often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' looks royal, but a queen is also a female cat, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A queen is a breeding female cat, so her diet would be cat food; the question mark flags the punning sense.

clue.text: More swanky citizenry relocated out of NYC, following Republican

indicators.note: the letters of that city's abbreviation are taken out of the fodder word
relocated things are moved to new positions, so the remaining letters are rearranged
following means coming after, so the shuffled part is placed behind the party abbreviation

blocks.note: R is the standard abbreviation for Republican
taken as written, before losing N, Y and C

explanation.surface: Wealthy citizens moving out of New York to somewhere posher, behind a Republican politician.
explanation.walkthrough: CITIZENRY loses N, Y and C to leave ITIZER, which is rearranged; 'following Republican' puts R first.
explanation.definitionFit: Ritzy, from the Ritz hotel, means luxurious and swanky; the comparative form matches 'more swanky'.

clue.text: Lectured at university in plaits

blocks.note: to be up is to be in residence at university
plaited hair is braided

explanation.surface: A student with plaited hair being lectured at college.
explanation.definitionFit: To upbraid someone is to scold or reprimand them, as a stern lecture does.

clue.text: Get hold of government file

blocks.note: G is a common abbreviation for government
a rasp is a coarse file for shaping wood or metal

explanation.surface: An instruction to obtain an official government document.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp something is to seize or take firm hold of it.

clue.text: Prison entertained by love song outside

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is taken into the host's home, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
pen is short for penitentiary, a prison
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A prisoner charmed by a love song sung outside the walls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside' looks like part of the picture but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-air event is held outdoors rather than under a roof, the adjectival sense of outside.

clue.text: Concern finding king asleep beneath throne

indicators.note: in a down answer, what lies beneath sits lower in the column, so it comes after the toilet word

blocks.note: the throne is jokey slang for the toilet, or loo
K is the chess abbreviation for king
someone out cold is asleep

explanation.surface: A worry about a monarch who has nodded off below his throne.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'beneath' puts K and OUT under LOO. The royal throne is really the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: In the idiom 'that's your lookout', a lookout is a person's own business or responsibility.

clue.text: Jack called Jill, perhaps a male bone was broken

indicators.note: something broken is smashed apart, so its letters fall into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, used in the fodder as well as the indicator

explanation.surface: A nursery-rhyme Jack and Jill tumble, and someone's bone gets broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Was' does double duty, both in the fodder and with 'broken'. A Jack, or jack tar, is a sailor; a female one might be called Jill.
explanation.definitionFit: An able seaman is a rated sailor; a woman holding that rank, a female Jack, is an able seawoman.

clue.text: Hot relaxing place, reflected by bar and hotel bill

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror is back to front, so the words are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: but means except, as in 'all but' or 'bar none'
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a tab is a bill, as in a bar tab

explanation.surface: A sunny spot to unwind, mirrored by the hotel bar and its bill.
explanation.walkthrough: BUT, H and TAB together are read backwards. 'Bar' wants to be a pub; here it means 'except'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bathtub filled with hot water is a place where people lie back and relax.

clue.text: A little Bonjela gel on gums lasting forever

indicators.note: a little of the following words means only a small portion of them, the run of letters straddling them

blocks.note: the letters run across Bonjela, gel, on and gums

explanation.surface: Advice to dab a little teething gel on sore gums for lasting relief.
explanation.walkthrough: Bonjela is a UK brand of mouth-ulcer and teething gel.
explanation.definitionFit: Agelong means lasting for an age, very long or seemingly endless.

clue.text: Religious leaders tormented legendary Son

indicators.note: something tormented is twisted and racked, so its letters are wrenched into another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Clerics persecuting a son of legend, perhaps a biblical one.
explanation.walkthrough: The General Synod is the governing assembly of the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: The General Synod is the national assembly of bishops, clergy and laity that governs the Church of England.

clue.text: Weird stuff to do with ears in short test

indicators.note: something short is cut down, so the last letter of the word for a test is dropped
in places one piece inside the other, which goes around it

blocks.note: an exam is a test
otic is the adjective for things relating to the ear

explanation.surface: A brief hearing examination turning up something odd.
explanation.walkthrough: EXAM loses its M to become EXA, which holds OTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Exotica are strange or unusual objects, especially from foreign places, so weird stuff.

clue.text: Head of the Academy showing Oscar- winning war film

blocks.note: Plato founded and led the Academy in ancient Athens
a film on is one being shown

explanation.surface: A film academy head screening a war picture that won an Oscar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Academy' suggests the Oscars, but here it is Plato's school of philosophy.
explanation.definitionFit: Platoon, Oliver Stone's 1986 Vietnam film, won the Academy Award for Best Picture.

clue.text: Seabirds pass over again to the west

definitions.note: plural; eider is also used unchanged as its own plural

indicators.note: in an across answer, heading west means going right to left, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: re- is the prefix for again
to pass over is to die

explanation.surface: Seabirds flying over a second time, heading westward.
explanation.definitionFit: The eider is a large sea duck of northern coasts, prized for its down.

clue.text: Bother covering green with yellow? One might be asked to

indicators.note: a cover goes over and around what it covers, so one word surrounds the other

blocks.note: drat is a mild curse, like bother!
eco- means environmentally friendly, or green
or is gold or yellow in heraldry

explanation.surface: Annoyance at painting over green with yellow; a professional might be hired for it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the wordplay: covering green with yellow is exactly what a painter might be asked to do. Or is the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter and decorator is hired to repaint rooms, such as covering green walls in yellow.

clue.text: Speck of blood, page with crumbs on — strange clues

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed on top of, so that piece comes first
strange means odd or out of the ordinary, so the letters take an unusual order

blocks.note: crumbs! and cor! are both exclamations of surprise
P is the abbreviation for page
taken as written

explanation.surface: A blood spot on a page covered in crumbs, beside some odd crossword clues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crumbs' is not breadcrumbs but the British exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A corpuscle is a single blood cell, a tiny particle in the bloodstream.

clue.text: Bloody bar brawl about syntax?

indicators.note: about can mean turned about, facing back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: blood is red
a rod is a bar
a row is a noisy fight or quarrel

explanation.surface: A violent pub fight that broke out over a grammar point.
explanation.walkthrough: RED, ROD and ROW are written in a line and then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Syntax is the arrangement of words into sentences, which is to say the order words come in.

clue.text: Messy look of strange wizard

blocks.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange
a mage is a magician or wizard

explanation.surface: An odd wizard's dishevelled appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: A rummage is a disorderly search, turning things over untidily while looking for something.

clue.text: General expert starts on oranges — lots of pith

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so only each one's first letter is kept

blocks.note: the first letters of oranges, lots and of
the pith of an argument is its essence, its gist

explanation.surface: A specialist commenting that oranges have plenty of pith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pith' looks like orange peel; here it means the core of a matter.
explanation.definitionFit: An ologist is a jocular word for any expert in an -ology, a specialist in some branch of knowledge.

clue.text: Dissident book covered with tape wound round and round

indicators.note: a thing covered with something else is wrapped up inside it

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for book
a reel is a spool with tape wound round it

explanation.surface: A protester's banned book bound up in layers of tape.
explanation.walkthrough: B goes inside REEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebel opposes authority, as a dissident does.

clue.text: Spirited Romeo's outside taking drugs

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its edges, so only its first and last letters are kept

blocks.note: the first and last letters of Romeo
a user takes drugs, so using means taking them

explanation.surface: A lively Romeo is out on the street taking drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romeo' is the NATO alphabet for R, but here just its outer letters are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A rousing speech or song is stirring and full of spirit.

clue.text: Provincial capital's reported beauty unlikely to fade

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so what counts is how the words sound

blocks.note: a belle is a beautiful woman
fast colours do not run or fade

explanation.surface: A regional capital whose good looks are said to be lasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Provincial' refers to Northern Ireland, often called the Province.
explanation.definitionFit: Belfast is the capital of Northern Ireland, which is often called the Province in British usage.

clue.text: Old lady marks animal with a death's head — epic!

blocks.note: your old lady is slang for your mother, ma
M is the abbreviation for the German mark currency
the death's-head hawkmoth has a skull-like marking

explanation.surface: A grandmother noting an animal with a skull on it, an epic sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animal' suggests a mammal, which the answer is, but the death's head belongs to a moth.
explanation.definitionFit: Mammoth means enormous in scale, so on an epic scale.

clue.text: Viking in the papers I see twirling pike

indicators.note: twirling turns something round, so the letters face the other way

blocks.note: ah! is said when one understands, like 'I see'
the gar or garpike is a long-snouted fish like a pike

explanation.surface: A newspaper story about a Viking spinning a pike weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pike' looks like a weapon fit for a Viking but is the fish; only the 'I see' part is twirled.
explanation.definitionFit: Hägar the Horrible is a long-running newspaper comic strip about a Viking.

clue.text: Applying customs, America beginning to upset friendly nation

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for an adverb meaning according to custom

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: US is the United States
the opening letter of upset
an ally is a friendly nation

explanation.surface: America imposing tariffs and upsetting a friendly country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Customs' suggests import duties; here it means habits.
explanation.definitionFit: Usually means as a matter of habit or custom, how things are normally done.

clue.text: Moving in range?

indicators.note: moving letters shifts them out of place, so they settle in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A target coming within firing distance.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, since something moving in range is approaching; 'Moving' also signals the reshuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearing means approaching, as anything moving into range is doing.

clue.text: Towering city with elegant past

blocks.note: chic means stylish or elegant
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: A city of tall buildings with a stylish history.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicago is the birthplace of the skyscraper, a city famous for its tall towers.

clue.text: Commentator's right to stand by boxer

indicators.note: a commentator speaks rather than writes, so the words are taken as they sound when spoken

blocks.note: well can mean right or proper
to stand by is to wait

explanation.surface: A sports commentator's right to support a fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, 'well to wait' gives the boxing division.
explanation.definitionFit: A welterweight is a boxer in the class between lightweight and middleweight.
